profile.name: Sathiya Sudan
profile.title: AI Engineer
profile.headline: I build production AI for banking — multi-agent assistants, identity verification and compliance automation — alongside LLM agents, RAG and ML at scale.

paragraphs: I'm an AI Engineer with 5+ years across machine learning, data science and generative AI. Today I build production AI for a leading Indian private bank — multi-agent banking assistants over MCP, signature and face verification, liveness detection and V-KYC audit automation.

My path runs from classical ML in production — recommendation engines, fraud detection and customer segmentation on Azure Databricks — through a Master's in Data Science (with Distinction) at the University of Essex, to today's agentic and RAG-based applications.
I care about AI that is grounded and reliable: tool-grounded retrieval, hallucination control, observability with LangSmith, and models that are deployed behind real APIs, not left in notebooks.

projects.title: Student Offer-Letter Prediction
projects.summary: XGBoost classifier served via FastAPI inside a university decision-support system.
projects.problem: The University of Essex needed a consistent, data-driven way to assess which applicants should receive offer letters.

currentRole.intro: End-to-end AI systems for retail banking — from identity verification and fraud prevention to conversational banking and compliance automation.

items.name: AI Banking
challenge: Banking apps bury common tasks behind deep menus.
Tasks like transfers and fixed deposits must execute securely, in real time, with full user context.
approach: Host agent handles planning and delegation; specialist agents cover balance, fund transfer, fixed deposits, statements, spending and expenses.
Agents discover each other through an agent registry service and reach core systems through an MCP server wrapping mobile-banking APIs.
Auth layer with JWT validation, OAuth and session checks before any agent acts.
items.impact: Brings the bank to natural language: "just ask" — balance, transfers and FDs completed in seconds with personalised, context-aware responses.

items.name: VerifyX
challenge: V-KYC quality assurance was manual and sampling-based — most sessions were never reviewed.
Needed to catch compliance misses and fraud such as a third party coaching the customer.
approach: Perception layer: Whisper ASR optimised with ONNX Runtime for fast local transcription of agent and customer streams.
Reasoning layer: GPT-4o evaluates each compliance checkpoint — disclaimer consent, name confirmation, random-code check, PAN display and more.
Reviewer UI with synced video, live transcript, pass/fail checklist and downloadable audit report.
items.impact: Moved audits from manual sampling to 100% automated coverage, cutting audit time by 90% and surfacing coaching fraud.

items.name: Syahi
challenge: Very high precision required — a wrong match is costly.
Signatures vary for the same person; reference images are low quality.
Noise from seals, tables, printed text and placeholders.
approach: Separate custom models per stage: YOLOX for signature detection and extraction, Pix2Pix GAN for cleaning, MobileNetV2 for similarity matching.
Reference signature fetched via API by account number; output is matched / not matched with a confidence score.
items.impact: 97% precision and 80% recall in internal validation, returning a verified decision in about a second.

items.name: Face Match
challenge: Aadhaar photos are often 10+ years old and low quality versus sharp live selfies.
Small faces in large images defeat standard detectors.
approach: VGGFace2-trained, L2-normalised 512-D embeddings robust to ageing, expression and lighting.
Unsharp-mask preprocessing plus a MediaPipe detection cascade; recursive multi-region search for low face-to-image ratios.
Strict cosine-similarity threshold (0.65) to prevent false account takeovers.
items.impact: 98.39% accuracy, 95.24% precision, 94.35% recall and 94.77% F1 across 2,480 verification pairs.

items.name: Liveness Detection
challenge: High-quality printed-photo attacks and video replays on a second screen.
Must run in real time on mobile with low latency.
approach: DeepPixBiS pixel-wise supervision to spot print artefacts — ink dots and paper texture.
Screen-replay detection from 2D artefacts across three consecutive frames.
items.impact: 0% HTER on Replay-Mobile and 0.42% ACER on OULU-NPU benchmarks; 12.4% cross-dataset HTER.
